title: Proper direct-image hypotheses for continuous-map algebraic-closure coefficients
statement: Fix a prime ell and a positive-characteristic field k of characteristic different from ell. For a proper k-morphism p:X to Y of separated finite-type k-schemes, ProperLocalizingHypotheses holds for the condensed ring of ALL continuous maps into PadicAlgCl ell. Thus Rp_* preserves bounded constant-model constructible finite-Tor objects and every existing ambient discrete colimit indexed in Type(u+2) whose vertices lie in Loc(Dctf(X)). This is the algebraic-closure representative of det-sf-comp-proper-admissible-hypotheses; no coefficient isomorphism and no compactification are involved. The ring is not the finite-subextension-valued condensed ring.

source.place: Second paragraph, Proper direct image, with the recorded admissible coefficient convention.

proof.text: The separate proper constructibility theorem gives constructible cohomology for each Dctf generator K. A lower bound of K is preserved by the right-derived bounded-below comparison. If K is at most b, apply the uniform lower-tail estimate in degree q=b+c+1. Its lower truncation is K itself, so Rp_* K is at most b+c. Thus the image is bounded constructible. The target is noetherian, so det-sf-comp-continuous-algcl-constructible-tor gives finite Tor amplitude. Together these prove the first conjunct of ProperLocalizingHypotheses.

Use the uniform lower-tail bound. In degree q, the truncation projection K to tau_ge(q-c) K induces an isomorphism after H^q Rp_*. Truncation preserves coproducts and the family of truncations has a common lower bound. The generic qcqs bounded-below continuity theorem preserves their coproduct. Naturality on each coprojection gives a commutative square; its other three sides are invertible, so the H^q coproduct comparison is invertible. Cohomology detects isomorphisms. The generic truncation/coproduct argument is proved locally, without importing the ell-adic proper-localizing theorem.

For any existing larger coproduct, its nonzero summands inject into its endomorphisms via the associated coordinate idempotents. Shrink that support to Type(u+1), apply the small coproduct assertion, and restore the zero summands. Additivity preserves zero objects. The resulting cocone has exactly the images of the original coprojections, proving preservation for the required Type(u+2) diagrams. Both the support estimate and the reindexing argument are proved locally; the compact-test right-adjoint theorem is not used.

proof_origin.place: Proper finiteness plus the separate uniform lower-tail bound; the bounded-below coproduct, cohomology and indexing-universe assembly is proved in Lean.

lean.statement:
theorem properLocalizingHypotheses_continuousAlgCl
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [Fact (ringChar k).Prime] [Fact (ringChar k ≠ ℓ)]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    (p : X ⟶ Y) [p.IsOver (Spec (.of k))] [IsProper p] :
    ProperLocalizingHypotheses
      (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj (PadicAlgCl ℓ)) p
